scope.vehicles: haulage and flat trucks treated as one; closed-body / canter and Hiab excluded; 3rd-party trucks included
scope.rule: only routes where 2+ clients ran trips in the same quarter are compared

methodology: Best rate = the highest rate any client paid on the same route and quarter
Best client average = the average rate of the best-paying client (by average) on that route and quarter
Rate level = client average ÷ best client average
Revenue lost = MAX(0, best client average − client average) × client trips (the "estimated rate opportunity" of the brief)
Lost if at highest = (highest rate on route − client average) × trips (the aggressive benchmark)
Turnaround: trips one truck can do per month = MAX(1, INT(operating days ÷ round-trip days)); round trip = 2 × one-leg days; trucks needed = trips ÷ trips per truck, rounded up per client
summaryText: Trips 2 Jan – 30 Sep 2026 · selling price excl. VAT · payment status ignored · haulage and flat trucks only (treated as one); closed-body/canter and Hiab trips excluded
Revenue if every trip had been sold at the best (highest) rate on its route: ₦2,569,440,468 — ₦178,325,327 more (+7.5%)
Revenue at the best-paying client’s average rate: ₦2,509,970,801 — ₦118,855,660 more (+5.0%). Detail by client and month: ‘Achieved vs Best Rate’ sheet.
Rate level = what a client pays compared with the best-paying client on the same route in the same quarter. 100% = pays the top rate.
Revenue lost = extra revenue if the client had paid the best-paying client’s average rate on those trips.
Total revenue lost to lower rates: ₦118.9M (5.0% of 2026 haulage revenue of ₦2.39bn).
Worst on rates: Jamara — pays ~89% of the best rate but, on high volume, costs ₦52.9M (45% of the total).
Second: Mega Manu — ~90% of the best rate, ₦23.8M lost. Jamara + Mega Manu = ₦76.7M.
Cheapest rate among sizeable clients: Lacasera at ~65% of the best rate (Lagos → Benin, Q1), ₦14.2M lost. Its Benin rate was raised to ₦1.63M by Q3.
Best on rates: SASO pays the top rate on every shared route, including the highest Lagos → Kano price every quarter. Natural Beauty (98%) and Givanas (97%) are close.
Act first on Jamara and Mega Manu’s Kano, Abuja and Ibadan rates — use SASO and Interstyle rates as the reference.
Only routes where 2+ clients ran trips in the same quarter are compared. Rates rose ~20–25% from Q1 to Q2, so comparisons stay within a quarter.
Some differences may have reasons not in the trip log (load weight, waiting time, contract terms). Review the largest gaps with each account.
